summary: Proceed, but only after retargeting the pooler warm-up: since small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl landed, master's pooler at T<=32 reads state["dl"]["w_pr"] (a separate bf16 [4608,8192] copy), not dense["pooler"]. Built as written, 25 MB of the warm-up would load a buffer nothing reads and pin it evict_last in L2, so a loss would wrongly mark the knob as dead.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. Every timed replay starts with a cold L2. On sliding T<=32 shapes the qk_norm/store/FA3(2048-window, <=8 MB KV)/o_norm_gate phase moves little DRAM traffic. The o GEMM and kernel P (pooler+router, 75.5 MB) right after it are HBM-bound. A 42 MB warm-up fits under the 50 MB L2, and FINDINGS shows those rows are material: dl_pooler_router_kernel is 23.9 us at sliding decode_16, 28.3 at decode_32 and 22.5 at verify_1. The o GEMM shares nvjet rows with the unpooler: 64x16 at 26.5 us at decode_16, 64x32 at 28.6 at decode_32, and 128x8 splitK at 12.8 at verify_1. The hypothesis text is stale, though. It cites the old nvjet 128x16 splitK pooler row (20.0 us) and incumbents of 230/270/205 us. The current numbers are 217.1/247.0/186.5 us, and at T<=32 the pooler is kernel P over dl["w_pr"]. The pooler view must therefore be dl["w_pr"][:1536] (rows 0..1535 are pooler rows in the same order), falling back to dense["pooler"][:1536] only when state["dl"] is None. Expected sizes: o is ~20% of its nvjet row (16.8 of ~84 MB at T=16/32), so warming it saves ~2-3 us. Kernel P is a single wave (216 CTAs at 2/SM) that is bandwidth-bound on total bytes, so removing 25 MB of 75.5 MB from HBM could save ~5-7 us if the lines survive. That is -5..-9 us on the three sliding shapes, ~+2-4% each. The headline effect is only ~0.5-1% (3 of 6 loads, sliding share ~2/3 of each load), inside the +-1.5% CI, so the result must be read from the profile rows (P row, o/unpooler nvjet row, the two warm rows, the FA3 row) and not from the headline. WEAKEST LINK: whether 32 programs can pull 42 MB (needs ~1.7-2 TB/s, i.e. ~55-65 GB/s per SM with plain tl.load) inside a sliding attention phase that is probably shorter than the assumed 25-30 us. If the warm-up is still running when the o GEMM and P start, it competes for HBM and keeps up to 32 SMs busy. P is sized as exactly one wave at 2 CTAs/SM, so leftover warm CTAs can push some P CTAs into a second wave. Under-delivery or a loss is the likely failure mode, and the warm rows' own duration in the profile is the deciding number. A second risk is the line survival budget: 42 MB of evict_last lines, plus 8 MB of concurrent KV traffic, plus o_norm_gate/boundary activations, sits right at the 50 MB capacity.
confounders: small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (landed, the base): changes which buffer the pooler reads at T<=32 (dl["w_pr"] instead of dense["pooler"]), so the change as written warms a dead buffer. Kernel P also already issues 3 weight stages per CTA (~10 MB chip-wide) before griddepcontrol.wait, overlapping part of the weight stream with the predecessor, so the warm-up's marginal gain on P is smaller than against the old nvjet pooler. P's single-wave sizing (216 CTAs at 2/SM) is sensitive to warm CTAs still being resident. If P were absent or OFF (self-check fail, logged as [small-t-dense-chain] OFF), the right target and the size of the gain both change, so the build must log which buffer it warmed.
sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: the side-stream router/pooler split it introduced no longer runs at T<=32 (superseded by P), so it does not confound inside the gate.
fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: full layers only (window == 0), outside the sliding gate; it does not confound, and full layers at the same T serve as an in-run control.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t and marlin-block-m-cap-16: run after the o and pooler GEMMs and read different weights. The only possible interaction is evict_last lines left in L2 during Marlin/unpooler, which are pure streams that gain little from L2. Not a meaningful confounder.
interference: No companion is warranted. The gate is config-only and limited to three sliding shapes. The same-T full-layer shapes and every T=1/T>32 shape are byte-for-byte master in the same run, so they act as built-in controls. Attribution comes from per-kernel profile rows: the P row (pooler part), the o/unpooler nvjet row (the unpooler is untouched, so any delta is o), and the two _l2_warm_kernel rows and their duration against the FA3/o_norm_gate rows. Together these separate the mechanisms. A gain shows up as a shorter P and o row. A loss splits into three readable cases: warm rows longer than the attention phase (HBM/SM contention, a longer FA3 row), P running slower than master (a second wave or contention), or P unchanged (lines evicted). An ab-revert of small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl would test the pooler part against a different kernel and buffer that is no longer master's path, which is not useful. An o-only control would only separate o from the pooler, which the rows already do. The headline will probably sit inside the CI either way, so judge the run on the rows, not the headline.
rules_flags: No rule is broken as specified: it reads only prepare()-time constant weights, keeps nothing derived from inputs, stores to the sink only under a data-dependent device-side predicate (no host branch on values), adds no host sync, forks and joins the side stream with wait_stream inside capture (a pattern master already used), and does all the work inside the timed kernel_fn. Prefetching weights inside the timed call is not cold-L2 tampering. Do not move it into prepare() or outside kernel_fn.

Make sure the fork uses main = torch.cuda.current_stream() at call time (the capture stream), not a stream saved in prepare(). Keep the join so the capture closes. Do not add record_stream calls during capture.
open_questions: How long is the sliding attention phase on master now (qk_norm + store_cache + FA3 + o_norm_gate rows at decode_16/32/verify_1)? If it is under ~20 us, consider warming only the o weight plus fewer pooler rows (e.g. 16.8 + ~12 MB) so the warm-up reliably finishes before the o GEMM.
Does the warm-up grid of 32 programs reach ~2 TB/s? Watch the _l2_warm_kernel row durations. 64 programs with smaller per-program ranges may be needed, at the cost of more SM pressure on FA3.

Which pooler rows should be warmed for kernel P? All 216 CTAs run in one wave and each streams a K-chunk of 64 rows, so warming rows 0..1535 makes 24 of 72 n-tiles cheap while the rest still set the HBM-bound tail. Total bytes saved is what matters, but check that P's row drops by roughly 25 MB / ~3.3 TB/s ≈ 7 us.

Overlap with the queued sliding-fused-batched-decode-port (shorter attention window to hide in) and prefork-qkv-o-swapab-t16-t32 (a different o kernel). Whichever lands first changes this one's budget, so re-baseline before stacking.
